details.body:
Remedies implementation

Timetables

The CMA’s final report stated that our remedies package will be introduced by Orders placing requirements on veterinary businesses and Undertakings offered by (or Orders imposed on) the RCVS during an implementation period of up to 6 months. On 20 August 2026, we made an Order (and accepted Undertakings from the RCVS) to establish a levy on veterinary businesses to enable the payment of relevant monies to the RCVS by those businesses, as soon as possible. This levy will fund preparatory and ongoing activities of the RCVS implementing the actions we are requiring of it. On 22 September, we made an Order to put in place the rest of our remedies package that applies to veterinary businesses and accepted Undertakings from the RCVS to support these remedies.

A timetable for each of these periods is set out as follows:

Funding Order and Undertakings

Date Activity
24 March 2026 Final report published
March to May 2026 Drafting of Funding Order and Undertakings, and informal consultation on them with key stakeholders
30 June 2026 Publication of draft Funding Order and Undertakings for formal consultation
July to August 2026 Finalise and make Funding Order and accept the Undertakings
20 August 2026 Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026 published
23 September 2026 Statutory deadline for implementing remedial action

Substantive Order and Undertakings

Date Activity
24 March 2026 Final report published
April to June 2026 Drafting of substantive Order and Undertakings, and informal consultation on them with key stakeholders
July 2026 Publication of draft substantive Order and Undertakings for formal consultation
August to September 2026 Finalise and make substantive Order and accept the Undertakings
22 September 2026 Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Undertakings 2026 published
23 September 2026 Statutory deadline for implementing remedial action

(*) UK vets sector timetable for remedies infographic (PDF, 94KB) (24.3.26)

The CMA has published explainers to help veterinary businesses that provide care to household pets understand what they need to do, and by when, in order to comply with the CMA’s Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026.

Large and small businesses will need to make the same changes, but smaller businesses will have longer to make them.

  • Small veterinary businesses: complying with the CMA’s Order
  • Large veterinary businesses: complying with the CMA’s Order

Compliance reporting form for veterinary businesses providing outsourced out-of-hours services

15 October 2026: Veterinary businesses that provide outsourced out-of-hours services to First Opinion Practices must tell the CMA that they are compliant with Articles 19(4) and 19(5)(a) and (b).

  • Tell the CMA you’re compliant with the Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026

Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Undertakings 2026

22 September 2026: The CMA has published the final: 

  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026 
  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Undertakings 2026   

Veterinary business must now get ready to introduce these changes. The first phase of measures will come into force for larger veterinary businesses from 23 December  2026, with further remedies being introduced in phases over the following months. Smaller veterinary businesses will have longer to make changes.

Commenting on the milestone, Martin Coleman, Chair of the independent Inquiry Group, said:

“Today marks a significant milestone in the biggest reform of veterinary services in a generation. Our reforms are now law and will make a difference to the millions of pet owners across the UK.

“By the end of this year, many pet owners will know upfront the cost of basic services like consultations and vaccinations and receive clear breakdowns of pet care plans. More changes will follow in the coming months, for example, pet owners will receive written estimates in advance for higher cost treatments.

“Our package of reforms will help pet owners better manage their budget and care for their pets, strengthen competition and improve trust in the veterinary sector.”

Publication date of substantive Order and Undertakings 

21 September 2026: The CMA intends to publish the substantive Order and Undertakings in its market investigation into veterinary services for household pets in the UK on Tuesday 22 September 2026. The Order and Undertakings will be available on this case page once published.

Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026

20 August 2026: The CMA has published the final:

  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026
  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026

Consultation on draft substantive Order and Undertakings

21 July 2026: The CMA has published for consultation the draft Veterinary Services Market Investigation Order 2026, a draft Explanatory Note to this Order, and the draft Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons Undertakings 2026.

In the final report, the inquiry group decided that a series of remedies would be imposed on veterinary businesses to address competition problems found in relation to the supply of veterinary services for household pets. Additionally, the inquiry group decided that the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS) would be well placed to perform certain activities to support the remedies to be imposed on veterinary businesses and to monitor compliance by those businesses with those remedies. The purpose of the draft Order and draft Undertakings is to give effect to the inquiry group’s decisions in the Final Report, and therefore remedy, mitigate or prevent competition problems in this sector.

The consultation closed at 23:59pm on 20 August 2026.

  • Consultation: Vets market investigation: draft substantive Order and Undertakings

Consultation on draft Funding Order and Undertakings

30 June 2026: The CMA has published for consultation the draft:

  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026
  • Explanatory Note to this Order
  • Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026

In the final report, the inquiry group decided that the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (RCVS) would be best placed to perform certain activities to support the remedies to be imposed on veterinary businesses and to monitor compliance with those remedies, and that the RCVS’s costs of performing those activities should be met by veterinary businesses.  

The CMA consulted on these draft documents, including the level of the levy which will be payable by veterinary businesses to the RCVS to re-imburse the costs it will incur between March 2026 and March 2027 and the basis of its calculation. The amount of the proposed levy is in line with the figure that was foreseen in the final report published in March 2026.

The consultation on the draft Funding Order and Undertakings was open from 30 June to 30 July 2026. We have now published the consultation responses.

Revised administrative timetable

15 May 2026: The administrative timetable was updated on 15 May 2026 and provides revised timings for consultation on and finalisation of the funding Order and Undertaking. The administrative timetable for the substantive remedies Order and Undertaking is unchanged.

Inquiry group

15 May 2026: Martin Coleman (Inquiry chair), Susan Hankey and Keith Richards are the inquiry group members in the remedies implementation phase. Humphrey Battcock and Robin Cohen are no longer members of the Group.

Consultation on a market investigation reference

12 March 2024: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) published an update report and consulted on whether to launch a market investigation into veterinary services for household pets in the UK. Having considered responses to the consultation, the CMA has decided to make a market investigation reference into the supply of veterinary services for household pets in the United Kingdom.

The consultation closed at 5pm on 11 April 2024.

The CMA also published a report of market research commissioned during the market review.

  • Consultation on the proposal to make a market investigation reference into veterinary services for household pets in the UK (12.3.24)

  • Qualitative Research on Pet Owners’ Experiences of Buying Veterinary Services in the UK (PDF, 791KB) (12.3.24)

  • Press notice: CMA identifies multiple concerns in UK vets market (12.3.24)

Call for information

On 7 September 2023: the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) launched a call for information inviting pet owners, people who work in veterinary practices and people who supply products and services to the veterinary services market to share their thoughts on the veterinary market for pets.

This call for information was open for a period of six weeks.

  • Press notice: CMA launches review of vet sector (7.9.23)

Timetable

The consultation period closed at 5pm on 11 April 2024.

In a market investigation, an inquiry group is the independent panel that is required to decide whether there is a prevention, restriction, or distortion of competition. The phases of a market investigation are subject to statutory time limits. The CMA must generally conclude a market investigation in 18 months and implement remedies in six months.

Contact

VetsMI@cma.gov.uk

Please note, we are unable to provide any information beyond what is shared on our case page. You can subscribe to email alerts which will inform you when new information has been added to the case page.

If you are a member of the public contacting us, please be aware that the CMA has no powers to take action or open a case on behalf of an individual consumer or business (for example, to pursue compensation, intervene in disputes or provide advice). We also cannot engage in correspondence with everyone who contacts us, however, we may get in touch if we require any further information.

Personal information

Any personal data you provide us will be handled in accordance with our obligations under the UK General Data Protection Regulation and the Data Protection Act 2018. Our personal information charter sets out the standards you can expect from us when we collect, use or share personal data and provides details of your rights in relation to that data and how to contact us.

How we may use your information

We are carrying out this work under section 5 of the Enterprise Act 2002, which gives the CMA the power to obtain, compile and keep under review information about matters relating to its functions.
